semantic.how_to_run: Install the ml extra (pip install -e ".[dev,ml]", with the CPU-only PyTorch first on Linux as the README shows), then run python -m evals.run --semantic. The first run downloads the two models from Hugging Face, about 180 MB.

llm.how_to_run: To run it with your own key, put ANTHROPIC_API_KEY in the environment or in a local .env file (see the README), then run python -m evals.run --llm. It makes one parse call per job and up to LLM_MAX_SUGGESTIONS rewrite candidates per pair (20 by default), billed to that key, and writes every candidate to llm_candidates.json next to this report.

error_analysis.title: Years requirements cite no resume lines
error_analysis.observation: For a years-only requirement the report gives the years it counted but no lines, while the labels cite the role header lines. These items always miss in evidence recall, which is why recall is also shown without them.

examples.what: "5+ years of professional software or data engineering experience": labeled direct; the report cites no lines (8.9 years read).
"5+ years of professional software or data engineering experience": labeled direct; the report cites no lines (13.3 years read).
"5+ years of professional software or data engineering experience": labeled direct; the report cites no lines (7.9 years read).

error_analysis.title: Related experience needs matching by meaning
error_analysis.observation: In exact mode the app never returns adjacent, so related experience the labels mark adjacent (GitLab CI for GitHub Actions, Java for C#) comes out as gap, partial or needs_check. Matching by meaning is meant for these and wasn't run.

examples.what: "Experience with GitHub Actions": labeled adjacent, app gap (GitHub Actions missing).
"Experience with GitHub Actions": labeled adjacent, app gap (GitHub Actions missing).
"Knowledge of Guidewire or other insurance platforms": labeled adjacent, app partial (Guidewire missing, Insurance listed).

error_analysis.title: The status is right but the first lines cited aren't the labeled ones
error_analysis.observation: The status matches the label, but none of the report's first three lines is a labeled evidence line. Evidence is listed skill by skill, so the first lines can all come from one skill of the requirement, or from a broad skill such as ETL (matched by "data pipelines").

examples.what: "Experience building data pipelines on AWS or Azure": labeled direct, app direct; first line: experience line "Implemented CI/CD for data pipelines with Azure DevOps." (ETL via 'data pipelines').

"Minimum 3 years of hands-on Guidewire PolicyCenter or BillingCenter configuration": labeled direct, app direct; first line: experience line "Configured PolicyCenter 10 for homeowners and dwelling fire lines, including PCF screen..." (PolicyCenter via 'PolicyCenter').
"Background in the insurance industry": labeled direct, app direct; first line: experience line "Senior ETL Developer, Demo Insurance Group (Jun 2015 - Feb 2019)" (Insurance via 'Insurance').

error_analysis.title: Work the labels count as shown is found only in a summary or skills line
error_analysis.observation: The labels count the work as shown in a bullet, but the bullet describes it in other words, so exact matching finds the skill only in the summary or skills section, or not at all, and calls the requirement partial.

examples.what: "Background in the insurance industry": labeled direct, app partial (Insurance listed).
"Hands-on NLP experience, including transformer models": labeled direct, app partial (NLP listed, Transformer models demonstrated).
"Experience with LLMs and retrieval-augmented generation": labeled direct, app partial (LLMs missing, RAG demonstrated).

error_analysis.title: Requirements that name no catalog skill are left for a person to check
error_analysis.observation: The rule parser only finds skills from the skill catalog. A requirement whose tools or domain are outside it gets no skills, and a degree or certification requirement the app can't judge is left to a person, so exact matching marks it needs_check whether the resume proves it, lacks it or shows it in part.

examples.what: "Experience mentoring other developers": labeled direct; the parser found no catalog skill in it.
"Experience mentoring other developers": labeled gap; the parser found no catalog skill in it.

error_analysis.title: A related skill or a missing detail is counted as direct proof
error_analysis.observation: The catalog files some tools under a broader skill as well (JUnit and NUnit also count as Unit testing, GitHub and GitLab as Git), so a requirement that names the broad skill can be proven by a line that names another tool, and a domain word ("payments") counts wherever a work line uses it.

examples.what: "You should be comfortable writing unit tests with Jest or a similar framework.": labeled adjacent, app direct from the experience line "Wrote JUnit tests for the endpoint and fixed 12 bugs from the team backlog." (Unit testing via 'JUnit').

"Experience in payments or financial services": labeled adjacent, app direct from the header line "Integrated a payments provider and SMS notifications into the booking flow." (Payments via 'payments').

error_analysis.title: Faithful rewrites rejected by the fact checker
error_analysis.observation: The checker errs toward rejecting. A leadership word ("led" for "ran") counts as a bigger claim, and another catalog name for the same skill ("Kubernetes" for "K8s") counts as a new product name.

examples.what: "Moved nightly batch workers from EC2 instances to K8s CronJobs." became "Moved nightly batch workers from EC2 instances to Kubernetes CronJobs.": labeled faithful, checker rejected ("Kubernetes" looks like the name of an organization or product that isn't in the original line.).

"Mentored 4 developers and ran the team's design review meetings." became "Mentored four developers and led the team's design review meetings.": labeled faithful, checker rejected ("led" claims more responsibility than the original line does.).
